newsitem.title: USA: Kerrey to head Senate Democrat campaign committee.
newsitem.headline: Kerrey to head Senate Democrat campaign committee.

text.p: Sens. Robert Torricelli of New Jersey and Robert Kerrey of Nebraska Tuesday were named to chair the Senate Democratic Campaign Committee with the goal of regaining control of the chamber from Republicans in 1998.

Kerrey was chairman of the committee during the last two years and agreed to Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle's request to continue. Torricelli, who was elected to the Senate last November after 14 years in the House, was named vice chairman.

Kerrey told reporters he hoped to make Democrats competitive in the 1998 Senate elections. Democrats must defend 18 of the 34 seats at stake next year and need a net gain of at least five to overcome the current 55-45 Republican majority.
Democrats had a net loss of two Senate seats in last November's elections. The party that holds the White House traditionally loses seats in Congress during non-presidential election years.
"I'm honoured to be asked," Torricelli said. He was sworn in as a senator earlier in the day.
The campaign committee raises money and provides campaign funds for Democratic Senate candidates. There are similar committees for Senate Republicans and House Democratic and Republican candidates.
